findings.reason: A bounded red test showed an over-limit diff could leave a proposed record before the caller received file_too_large. Diff validation now precedes all private object/record writes, and the regression asserts both store directories remain empty.

A bounded red test showed create cleanup failure after a successful exclusive link was reported as zero-effect conflict even though the target existed. The mutation bit is now set immediately after replace/link, so later cleanup or fsync failures report file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=applied and preserve the writer claim.

The final suite exposed a test assertion that replayed an unchanged record and expected a quota error at exact capacity. The implementation correctly allows projected size == max_bytes; the regression now uses a larger recovery record and verifies the rejection boundary.

New-diff review found that secure-runtime admission checked descriptor-relative os.rename while record and target replacement called os.replace, which is not advertised in os.supports_dir_fd on the current runtime. A simulated ENOSYS replacement failed during prepared persistence before the fix; both call sites now use the checked descriptor-relative os.rename primitive and the regression passes.

A bounded red test showed that a candidate-object read failure after the durable prepared transition escaped as file_invalid_record, which suggested a zero-effect retry and released the recovery claim. The apply path now preserves the writer claim and reports file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=none when preparation cannot be completed; the target remains unchanged and the prepared record stays available for inspection.

Fresh-context review found that the new recovery handler called the fallible claim-preservation path before committing the no-release decision. If the store was unavailable, the raw store error could escape and finally could release the prepared lock after recovery. The handler now sets preserve_claim before attempting preservation, tolerates a preservation failure, and still returns file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=none; a mocked-outage regression covers the path.

New-diff review found an unpaired surrogate escaping as UnicodeEncodeError. The red regression reproduced the raw exception and stopped before its filesystem assertions; the fixed regression then asserted that the create target did not exist and records/objects were empty. The UTF-8 refusal itself occurs before proposal persistence.

Independent fresh-context review of fa9e54ef54d9c22e712526e04362898c28ec926c..d4510f113490604e7337812a96fe39a6a12eb758 identified that the uncaught red exception stopped before filesystem assertions. The record now attributes those assertions only to the fixed green run, rather than inventing red-stage execution.

A red real-filesystem regression for both replace and create observed candidate bytes at the target, then failed because post-commit FileChangeError was classified as file_conflict. After observed rename/link success, readback refusal now reports file_recovery_required/applied and preserves unresolved record/claim evidence; the new regression passes.

Red regressions observed the real applied file before failing on raw secondary FileChangeStoreError, including a receipt-time store rename/symlink replacement. Applied/unknown and receipt-error paths now set no-release intent before fallible preservation and contain secondary store errors, preserving the original recovery classification. Both regressions pass.

The first undo API draft required local approval and exact persisted identity but omitted the current write-path grant named by the approved contract. A red signature/behavior regression exposed the missing boundary; undo and session compensation now require write_paths, persist a zero-effect rejected event when revoked, and the regression passes.

A red restart regression showed session compensation returned undone with an empty list while the same session held undo_prepared plus a preserved writer claim after receipt failure. Session inventory now returns recovery_required before selecting any earlier applied change and reports the unresolved and remaining ids.

A red real-filesystem regression rewrote an unrelated undone receipt to name an earlier change and showed the first draft trusted the receipt field alone, accepting a same-hash replacement identity. Restored identities are now accepted only when the successor immutable before identity and digest independently recompute the same predecessor relation; the forged receipt is refused as file_conflict.

Exact-head PR #45 CI passed Ubuntu/macOS but both Windows jobs errored during test setUp because FileChangeStore intentionally refuses runtimes without descriptor-relative no-follow I/O. The implementation was correct; the new secure-filesystem suites lacked the portability admission pattern already used by evidence verifier tests. Secure file-change classes and the one tool helper test now skip only when the capability is absent, while a separate Windows-capable regression asserts FileChangeUnsupportedRuntime occurs before .pocketchat state is created.

why: PC-FILE-CHANGE-1 now requires the existing proposal/apply checkpoint and persistent undo/restart lineage to form one complete safe-file-change service.

The expanded package must reverse A-to-B-to-C as C-to-B-to-A, refuse arbitrary same-hash identity replacement, remove only an unchanged owned create, and stop session compensation at the first conflict or unresolved recovery state.
not_doing: No tool-contract registration, Session/CLI/UI/model wiring, default mutation entry, general delete surface, release version/tag/Release/package upload or paid provider action.
No automatic takeover of a preserved writer claim and no hostile-process/network-filesystem exactly-once claim.

pocketchat/file_changes.py: closed undo_prepared/undone transitions, exact current grant and target identity/hash checks, atomic restore or owned-create removal, durable receipt/idempotence, predecessor/successor lineage revalidation and dependency-safe session compensation.

tests/test_file_undo.py: real-filesystem replace/create, restart, chained undo, same-hash replacement, revoked grant, prepare/receipt failure, unresolved session state and forged successor-lineage regressions.
Existing proposal/apply/store/tool tests remain the earlier package evidence; bilingual file-work/security docs now describe the implemented library boundary without claiming a command surface.
static_checks: Undo cannot start without an explicit bounded approval identity and a current write-path grant.
Before mutation, undo persists undo_prepared with the exact candidate digest, observed identity, action and computed predecessor link.
Replace undo atomically restores the persisted before object and independently reopens it; create undo unlinks only the exact applied identity/hash and verifies absence.
A restored inode is trusted for the next undo only when the successor receipt and the successor immutable before identity both prove the predecessor relation.

Session compensation inventories persisted records after restart, computes reverse dependency order, stops on the first conflict and refuses to proceed past prepared/undo_prepared/recovery_required state.
Receipt-store failure after a real undo preserves undo_prepared plus the writer claim and reports file_recovery_required/applied; prepare persistence failure leaves target bytes unchanged.
The proposal helper remains unregistered; no model, CLI, Session or UI path can call apply or undo in this package.
Unsupported runtimes do not emulate weaker file I/O: secure filesystem suites are capability-gated and a separate regression proves FileChangeStore refuses before creating private state.
